newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN SURPLUS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN SURPLUS MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable amid excess liquidity on Thursday.
"It's very busy today but people are holding onto their paper because they are anticipating a fall in the treasury bill rate today because the market is in surplus," one dealer said.
He said discount houses were buying the central bank paper at 22.49 percent, the same as overnight, and selling at 22 percent from 22.25 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at Wednesday's 23.5 percent level and sold at an unchanged 22.75 percent, while call money was quoted at its previous 22 percent rate.

Bankers' acceptance bills were being bought at 22.75 percent, also unchanged from overnight and were selling at 22 percent compared to 22.50. The market opened in surplus of Z$600 million versus Z$223 million previously.
